title: Sheaves of modules on a small ringed site are Grothendieck abelian
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site whose underlying category is small and let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. The abelian category $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]: it has all small colimits, filtered colimits are exact, and the family of free sheaves $j_{U!}\mathcal O_U$ indexed by objects $U$ of $\mathcal C$ yields a generator $\bigoplus_{U\in\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal C}j_{U!}\mathcal O_U$, where $\mathcal O_U$ is the restriction of $\mathcal O$ to the localized site $\mathcal C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] and $j_{U!}\mathcal O_U$ is the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the extension-by-zero presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $P_{\mathcal O_U}$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf].

source.place: Section 07A5, first paragraph; Modules on Sites, Lemmas 03DA, 03DB, 03EW

proof.text: The category $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ is abelian by [lem-pur-ringed-site-module-category-abelian], applied to the small site $\mathcal C$ and the sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], all small colimits in $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ exist and are computed by sheafifying sectionwise colimits; the forgetful functor to abelian sheaves is faithful, exact, and commutes with these colimits.

For a filtered diagram of short exact sequences in $\Mod(\mathcal O)$, exactness of the forgetful functor and its commutation with colimits reduce exactness to filtered colimits in $\Ab(\mathcal C)$, which are exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact]. Thus filtered colimits in $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ are exact.

Let $G=\bigoplus_{U\in\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal C}j_{U!}\mathcal O_U$, which exists by step 2. If $q:\mathcal M\to\mathcal Q$ is a nonzero quotient, the epimorphism supplied by [lem-pc-sites-modules-quotient-j-shriek] for $\mathcal M$ implies that some component $h_{U,s}:j_{U!}\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal M$ has $q h_{U,s}\ne0$ (otherwise $q$ would vanish on the coproduct and hence be zero). Extend $h_{U,s}$ by zero on the other summands to a map $G\to\mathcal M$; its composite with $q$ is nonzero. Thus $G$ is a generator.

The abelian category $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ has all small colimits, exact filtered colimits, and the generator $G$ from step 4, so it is Grothendieck abelian by [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. The descriptions of $\mathcal O_U$ and $j_{U!}\mathcal O_U$ are exactly the localized-site restriction and sheafified extension-by-zero presheaf in the statement.

proof_origin.place: Lemmas 03DA, 03DB, 03EW, together with Cohomology on Sites Section 07A5
